title: SN1 and SN2 energy profiles
caption: SN2 has one transition state and no intermediate. SN1 has two transition states with a carbocation intermediate in the valley between them; the first barrier is the highest, so ionisation is the rate-determining step.
alt: Two energy profiles. SN2: a single hump. SN1: two humps with a carbocation intermediate in the dip between them, the first hump higher.
description: Left panel, SN2: energy rises from the reactants to a single transition state, marked with a double dagger, then falls to the products, which are lower in energy than the reactants. The activation energy is marked from the reactants to the top of the hump.

Right panel, SN1: energy rises to a first, higher transition state (ionisation), falls into a shallow dip holding the carbocation intermediate, rises to a second, lower transition state (nucleophile attack), then falls to the products. The activation energy of step 1 is marked; it is the largest barrier, so step 1 is rate-determining.
